quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. Time phrases come at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + drinks (verb) + milk (object) + every morning (time). Time expressions like 'every morning' usually appear at the end of a sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. The manner adverb comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + reads (verb) + a book (object) + quietly (manner). Adverbs of manner like 'quietly' follow the verb and its object.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The cat'. 'All day' is a time expression.
quests.explanation: Subject (The cat) + sleeps (verb) + all day (time). 'All day' means for the entire day, and naturally ends the sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'My'. The object is a type of food.
quests.explanation: Subject (My sister) + loves (verb) + chocolate cake (object). 'Chocolate' acts as an adjective here, describing the type of cake.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The dog'. 'Very' comes before the adverb.
quests.explanation: Subject (The dog) + barks (verb) + very loudly (manner). 'Very' is an intensifier placed before 'loudly' to strengthen its meaning.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'We'. 'Games' is the object; 'on weekends' tells us when.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + play (verb) + games (object) + on weekends (time). 'On weekends' uses 'on' for recurring days or time periods.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'To school' tells us where he goes.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + goes (verb) + to school (place) + early (time). 'Early' here means he arrives before the usual time.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. The base verb 'cook' comes last.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + helps (verb) + her mother (object) + cook (base verb). 'Help someone + base verb' is a natural English pattern.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The children'. Two verbs are joined by 'and'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The children) + sing (verb 1) + and + dance (verb 2). Two verbs joined by 'and' describe two simultaneous or related actions.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'I'. 'At noon' is a time expression.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + eat (verb) + lunch (object) + at noon (time). 'At' is used with specific times: at noon, at midnight, at six o'clock.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The rain'. 'Heavily' describes the manner; 'today' ends it.
quests.explanation: Subject (The rain) + falls (verb) + heavily (manner) + today (time). When both manner and time appear, manner usually comes before time.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Birthday' describes the type of gift.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + opens (verb) + her birthday gift (object). 'Birthday' acts as an adjective modifying 'gift', describing its occasion.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Daily' is a frequency adverb at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + cleans (verb) + his room (object) + daily (frequency). 'Daily' means every day and acts as a frequency adverb.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Always' comes before the main verb 'eat'.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + always (adverb) + eat (verb) + dinner (object) + together (manner). Frequency adverbs like 'always' sit between the subject and the main verb.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The teacher'. 'A story' is the object.
quests.explanation: Subject (The teacher) + reads (verb) + a story (object). 'A' is the indefinite article used before a singular, countable noun like 'story'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'In her diary' tells us where.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + writes (verb) + in her diary (place). 'In' is used for enclosed or contained spaces: in a diary, in a notebook.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The bus'. 'At seven' is the time.
quests.explanation: Subject (The bus) + arrives (verb) + at seven (time). 'At' is the correct preposition with specific clock times.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Twice' means two times and ends the sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + brushes (verb) + his teeth (object) + twice (frequency). 'Twice' means two times and usually appears at the end of the sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The flowers'. 'In spring' uses 'in' with seasons.
quests.explanation: Subject (The flowers) + bloom (verb) + in spring (time). 'In' is always used with the four seasons: in spring, in summer, in autumn, in winter.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Daily' is a frequency adverb at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + waters (verb) + her plants (object) + daily (frequency). 'Water' as a verb means to give water to plants - a common action.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Well' is the adverb form of 'good'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + plays (verb) + the guitar (object) + well (manner). 'Well' is the adverb form of 'good' - never say 'plays good'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'They'. 'At the beach' is the location.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + swim (verb) + at the beach (place). 'At' is used with specific locations like 'the beach', 'the park', 'the office'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The baby'. 'In the afternoon' uses 'in' with time of day.
quests.explanation: Subject (The baby) + sleeps (verb) + in the afternoon (time). Time of day phrases - morning, afternoon, evening - all use 'in'.
quests.textToSpeak: The baby sleeps in the afternoon.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Beautiful' comes before 'pictures'. 'Often' ends the sentence.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + paints (verb) + beautiful pictures (object) + often (frequency). Adjectives like 'beautiful' always directly precede the noun they describe.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'At the bakery' tells us where.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + buys (verb) + bread (object) + at the bakery (place). 'At' is used with shops and public establishments.
quests.textToSpeak: He buys bread at the bakery.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The sun'. 'In the east' uses 'in' with directions.
quests.explanation: Subject (The sun) + rises (verb) + in the east (place). 'In' is used with compass directions: in the north, in the south, in the east, in the west.
quests.textToSpeak: The sun rises in the east.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'She'. 'Every day' is a time expression at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + calls (verb) + her friend (object) + every day (frequency). 'Every day' (two words) means each day. Compare 'everyday' (one word) = ordinary.
quests.textToSpeak: She calls her friend every day.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'We'. 'Movies' is the object; 'on weekends' tells us when.
quests.explanation: Subject (We) + watch (verb) + movies (object) + on weekends (time). 'On' is used with days and parts of days: on Monday, on weekends, on Friday evenings.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'He'. 'Broken' is an adjective before 'chair'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + fixes (verb) + the broken chair (object). 'Broken' is a past participle used as an adjective to describe the state of the chair.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The dog'. 'Happily' is a manner adverb at the end.
quests.explanation: Subject (The dog) + fetches (verb) + the ball (object) + happily (manner). 'Happily' is the adverb form of 'happy', showing how the dog performs the action.
quests.textToSpeak: The dog fetches the ball happily.
